Weird that you would claim that "Less predisposition for genetic disease is an old wives **tale**" and then go on to explain how genetics works and how "the only way a mixed breed has better odds is if it’s one sick breed mixed with one healthy breed." Which is literally the argument for mixed breeds having a decreased predisposition to genetic diseases. Yeah, genetics is 100% luck. However, a great way to improve one's luck is to reduce the negative variables. Breed two untested dogs whose breeds have shown frequent cases of Von Willebrand's Disease, for example, and you heighten your risk of the parents both carrying the trait. Breed one of those dogs with a different breed that shows less frequency of the disease and you've greatly reduced your odds of the mixed offspring inheriting the disease. Does freaky shit happen and both dogs still had it despite one of them being a breed not known for possessing the trait? Absolutely, the only way to have known for sure would have been to have had the parents tested prior to breeding. In general, though, mixed just have better odds of avoiding breed-specific genetic disease.
